exercise.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
library_steps: Set both pulleys low and hold a handle in each hand.
Step forward with your elbows a little bent.
Sweep the handles up and together at chest height.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing between two low pulleys with a D-handle in each hand; the softly bent arms sweep from low and wide up and together in front of the chest at chest height. Chest (upper fibres) does the work; the front delt helps.

setup.target: Both low (~0.1 m), the athlete a little in front of them.

movement.measure: upper arm from the side line

muscles.emg: Main mover of the fly (S1); front delt only ~19 % MVIC in the fly (S2).
muscles.role: Brings the arm across the body; what the exercise is for.
Helps bring the arm forward; library secondary.

muscles.emg: Antagonist holding the elbow in the fly (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows bend and the hands push forward.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Fly form keeps the elbows fixed.

mistakes.mistake: Hands above the head at the end

sources.citation: Solstad TEJ, Andersen V, Shaw M, et al. 2020. A comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males. J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651.
sources.what_it_gave: Dumbbell fly vs bench press, 6RM: pectoralis major the main mover in the fly; front delt active; biceps works as an antagonist holding the slightly bent elbow.

sources.citation: Campos YAC, Vianna JM, Guimaraes MP, et al. 2020. Different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals. J Hum Kinet 75:5-14.
sources.what_it_gave: Bench press, dumbbell fly, shoulder press, lateral raise at 60 % 1RM: front delt only ~19 % MVIC in the fly; side delt highest in the lateral raise (30 %).

clip_check.check: End: hands together in front of the chest at chest height
Both fists closed on the handles; cables to the low pulleys clear of the arms
